bihar_raw_news.title: United Breweries gets BIADA nod to restore 42-acre Bihar land allotment
bihar_raw_news.content: Corporate & Business 2 min Read United Breweries gets BIADA nod to restore 42-acre Bihar land allotment The restoration follows the company's application under Bihar's Amnesty Policy 2025 after the industrial authority cancelled the original allotment in 2022 over non-operational status and non-utilisation of the land. Online Desk ETLegalWorld Published On Nov 14, 2026 at 08:46 PM IST Set ETLegalWorld as your preferred source on Google Share Icon Copy Link Share on Whatsapp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook Bookmark Comment United Breweries Ltd (UBL) has received final approval from the Bihar Industrial Area Development Authority (BIADA) for restoration of its 42-acre leasehold land at Kopakalan Industrial Area in Patna under the state's Amnesty Policy 2025 . The company disclosed the development in a regulatory filing dated November 14 under Regulation 30 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India 's (SEBI) Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements Regulations, 2015. UBL was allotted Plot No. A-1, measuring 42 acres, by BIADA in 2011 to establish a brewery . The unit subsequently commenced operations. However, following the implementation of Bihar's prohibition policy, the company was forced to discontinue beer production and later secured approval to change the product category from beer to non-alcoholic beverages . During periodic inspections, BIADA found the unit to be non-operational. The authority subsequently cancelled the land allotment and lease in 2022, citing the unit's non-operational status and non-utilisation of the allotted land. UBL challenged the cancellation before the Patna High Court, which passed a status quo order concerning the land. The proceedings remained pending before the court. Subsequently, following the introduction of BIADA's Amnesty Policy 2025, UBL applied for restoration of the allotment, submitted the requisite documents and compliances, and withdrew its writ proceedings. BIADA has now issued an office order restoring the allotment, subject to specified conditions. These include submission of a compliance and acceptance letter within 15 days, achieving trial production within 18 months and commercial production within 24 months. The company is also required to obtain the necessary statutory approvals, furnish details of project financing and implementation, pay applicable charges and comply with BIADA's conditions governing land utilisation. The restoration will entail annual land lease charges of ₹14.62 lakh and facilities charges of ₹70,800, in addition to restoration costs, the company said. UBL added that the communication formally conveys BIADA's approval for restoration and sets out the conditions to be fulfilled by the company. Comments What are your thoughts?

bihar_raw_news.title: Has ₹43,060 crore cleaned the Ganga in 10 years? Govt counters Bloomberg report on ...
bihar_raw_news.content: Has ₹43,060 crore cleaned the Ganga in 10 years? Govt counters Bloomberg report on persistent pollution A decade after Namami Gange was launched, questions remain over whether ₹ 43,060 crore has made the Ganga cleaner. A Bloomberg investigation flags persistent pollution, while the government defends its progress, citing improved water quality in some stretches and expanded sewage-treatment capacity. Bhanu Pratap Published 14 Nov 2026, 08:11 PM IST Prefer Livemint on Google Namami Gange Programme being held at the banks of river ganga in bihar.// photo by priyanka parashar AI Quick Read A decade after the launch of the Namami Gange programme, questions remain over whether the government's investment in cleaning the Ganga has made a significant difference to its water quality. A recent Bloomberg investigation, based on 10 years of satellite data covering nearly 2,000 km of the river and independent water tests, found that large stretches remain polluted despite the government spending ₹ 43,060 crore on the cleanup programme. The investigation looked at changes in turbidity, algae and surface temperature, along with water samples collected from 12 locations around Kanpur and Varanasi . Its findings raised questions about whether the money spent and infrastructure created have translated into a cleaner river. The government has defended the programme, arguing that the investigation does not capture the condition of the entire river. It says water quality has improved in several stretches, sewage-treatment capacity has increased and industrial pollution has declined. However, it has also acknowledged that pollution continues in parts of Uttar Pradesh , sewage-treatment capacity remains inadequate in some areas and stronger enforcement is needed. The findings point to a mixed picture: there has been progress in some stretches, but cleaning the Ganga remains a work in progress. What did the Bloomberg investigation find? The Bloomberg investigation examined whether a decade of investment under Namami Gange had resulted in a measurable improvement in the river's health. It used satellite data to track turbidity, algae and surface temperature over time, along with independent water testing around Kanpur and Varanasi . The findings suggest that pollution remains a serious concern in several stretches. They also raise questions about whether the government's spending has delivered the expected environmental benefits. Also Read | Centre approves 8 projects worth ₹638 cr under Namami Gange The larger issue is how the success of a river-cleaning programme should be measured. Spending money and building sewage-treatment plants are important steps, but they do not automatically mean that the river is cleaner. The results must be visible in regular water-quality tests. Why the Ganga cannot be judged through a few samples The government argues that a river stretching nearly 2,500 km cannot be assessed through satellite observations and samples from just 12 locations. The Ganga flows through five states and passes through different geographical and climatic conditions. It also receives water and sediment from major tributaries, including the Yamuna , Ghaghara, Gandak, Kosi, Gomti and Son. bihar_raw_news.title: IICA convenes stakeholder consultation on future of public policy professionals - IANS LIVE
bihar_raw_news.content: IICA convenes stakeholder consultation on future of public policy professionals IANS November 14, 2026 7:49 PM Share on | New Delhi, Nov 14 (IANS) The Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs (IICA) has launched an initiative to help define the role of public policy professionals and strengthen capacity-building frameworks at the intersection of business and government, an official statement said on Saturday. The Ministry of Corporate Affairs-backed institution recently convened a stakeholder consultation, bringing together senior government officials, corporate executives, policy experts, academics and industry representatives to examine the evolving responsibilities of public policy and corporate affairs functions within organisations. The discussions focused on how companies engage with policymakers and regulators, the capabilities required for policy professionals and the development of learning pathways aligned with organisational needs and national priorities. Addressing the gathering, IICA Director General and Chief Executive Officer Gyaneshwar Kumar Singh highlighted the importance of sustained engagement between governments and businesses, saying stronger institutional capacity can support more informed policy dialogue and decision-making. Meanwhile, former senior bureaucrats and corporate leaders participating in the consultation called for closer collaboration between regulators and industry, greater predictability in policymaking and development of professionals capable of bridging the public and private sectors. They also noted that public policy functions are increasingly moving beyond traditional government liaison roles and are becoming strategic advisory functions that help organisations assess regulatory developments, manage stakeholder relationships and contribute to policy discussions. The consultation identified a range of competencies required for policy professionals, including an understanding of government decision-making processes, economic analysis, data-driven reasoning, risk assessment and stakeholder management. Notably, experts also highlighted the need to balance corporate objectives with broader public interest considerations. On education and skill development, participants recommended multidisciplinary and case-based training programmes, flexible learning models for working professionals and internship opportunities within government institutions to build practical experience. The event drew more than 50 senior representatives from listed and multinational companies, consulting firms, think tanks, industry associations, academia, civil society organisations and government departments. According to the ministry, the deliberations concluded with a roadmap for collaboration between IICA, industry bodies and academic institutions to support the professionalisation of public policy and corporate affairs roles, reflecting their growing importance in shaping corporate strategy and contributing to national development goals. --IANS ag/

bihar_raw_news.title: Premature menopause exposes gaps in women's healthcare | Policy Circle
bihar_raw_news.content: Millions of Indian women face premature menopause, but gaps in diagnosis, research and healthcare leave their needs neglected. Premature menopause needs urgent policy attention: A piece published in Hindustan Times last month highlighted how menopause has long been neglected as a public health issue in India, with implications for health policy, healthcare systems and research. There is a need to focus attention on a group that has received little attention: women who experience menopause before the age of 40. This article draws on data from the Longitudinal Ageing Study in India (LASI), a nationally representative survey of over 72,000 adults aged 45 and above, the largest such study conducted in India. Our analysis of more than 17,000 women in the LASI sample (2017–18) finds that over 5% had experienced premature menopause, defined here as natural menopause before the age of 40. Extrapolated to India’s older female population, this translates to an estimated eight million women living with the long-term health consequences of an early hormonal transition. Hysterectomy is treated as a separate outcome in our analysis. READ | Kerala’s missing male infertility data and ageing crisis Premature menopause as a public health problem A parallel study using NFHS-5 data puts the prevalence among currently married women aged 30–39 at nearly 5% in rural areas and 3% in urban areas, with a particularly high burden in Bihar, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. In states such as Bihar, a significant share of this burden may be associated with hysterectomy among women with less education rather than natural ovarian decline (Saha et al., 2024). The education gradient is striking, and sharper than earlier analyses suggested. Women with the lowest education levels are almost seven times more likely to experience premature menopause than those with the highest education: 6.85% compared with 0.94% (Saha et al., 2024). Decomposition analysis from the same study finds that 73% of this gap is explained by hysterectomy before the age of 40. The remaining gap is associated with poverty, early and repeated childbearing, and sterilisation, characteristics concentrated among women who undergo hysterectomy rather than necessarily independent causes of premature menopause. These findings change how we understand premature menopause at the population level in India. It is commonly discussed as a spontaneous biological event. Yet the Indian evidence points to a substantial surgical component, raising questions about procedures performed on women in their 30s, often without adequate information about their long-term consequences. Hysterectomy does not necessarily cause immediate menopause when the ovaries are preserved, but it may affect subsequent ovarian function. The clinical governance of hysterectomy therefore deserves attention in any examination of premature menopause. bihar_raw_news.title: Complete Patna Sahib-Patna Ghat link road within deadline: Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary to officials
bihar_raw_news.content: Complete Patna Sahib-Patna Ghat link road within deadline: Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary to officials ANI | Updated: Nov 14, 2026 20:14 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Patna (Bihar) [India], November 14 (ANI): Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Saturday inspected the under-construction 1.5-kilometre link road connecting Patna Sahib Railway Station to Patna Ghat under the JP Ganga Path project and directed officials to complete the work within the stipulated timeframe while ensuring high quality, a release said. During the inspection near Patna City, Road Construction Department Principal Secretary Pankaj Kumar Pal briefed the Chief Minister on the progress of the project. He informed that the link road is being built for Rs 52.54 crore, with construction work having commenced on April 5, 2025. Starting from Patna Sahib Railway Station, the link road connects to the Patna Ghat point of the JP Ganga Path and also includes the construction of a flyover on Ashok Rajpath. Highlighting the benefits of the project, Chief Minister Choudhary said the link road will ensure direct connectivity between Patna Sahib Railway Station and the JP Ganga Path, while helping ease traffic congestion in the Ashok Rajpath and Marufganj Mandi areas. He added that the project will improve road connectivity for Dalhatta, Charkhipar, and adjoining localities. Additionally, the JP Ganga Path will be linked to the new NH-30 via a Road Over Bridge (ROB) at Patna Sahib Railway Station. Reiterating the state government's commitment to providing better road infrastructure and traffic facilities to citizens, the Chief Minister stated that the link road will significantly ease commuting and streamline traffic movement for the residents of Patna City. Principal Secretary Pankaj Kumar Pal, Urban Development and Housing Department Secretary Animesh Parashar, Municipal Commissioner Yashpal Meena, District Magistrate Kundan Kumar, and other senior officials were present during the inspection. (ANI)

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Bridge Named Nitish Setu; PM Modi to Open on Nov 21 - The Open Press
bihar_raw_news.content: Politics Bihar Bridge Named Nitish Setu After Former Chief Minister as PM Modi Set to Inaugurate on November 21 Bihar has named its new six-lane bridge over the Ganga Nitish Setu, after Janata Dal (United) president and former chief minister Nitish Kumar. Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary announced the name on X… Published By : Politics Desk , Patna Last Updated: November 14, 2026, 14:15 IST The six-lane Kacchi Dargah-Raghopur-Bidupur bridge over the Ganga, which Bihar has named Nitish Setu after former chief minister Nitish Kumar. Bihar has named its new six-lane bridge over the Ganga Nitish Setu, after Janata Dal (United) president and former chief minister Nitish Kumar. Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary announced the name on X on Friday, saying Prime Minister Narendra Modi will dedicate the bridge to the nation on 21 November. The bridge connects Kacchi Dargah in Patna to Raghopur and Bidupur in Vaishali on the north bank of the Ganga. At 19.76 km including approach roads, with a main section of 9.76 km, it will be the longest river bridge in India, overtaking the 9.15 km Bhupen Hazarika Setu in Assam. A first for Bihar's longest-serving leader This will be the first major infrastructure project in Bihar to be named after Nitish Kumar, who stepped down as chief minister in April this year, handing over to Samrat Choudhary. The naming is widely seen as a gesture to keep a key alliance partner in good humour. JDU working president Sanjay Kumar Jha welcomed the decision. "Nitish Kumar has worked to restore Bihar's pride for the last 20 years... it's a matter of prestige for all of Bihar," he said. RJD MLA Ranvijay Sahu, however, called the naming an act of appeasement. A bridge years in the making The project was sanctioned in 2015, and its first phase, a 4.57 km stretch connecting Kacchi Dargah to Raghopur Diyara, was opened to public traffic on 23 June 2025. The full bridge is expected to ease traffic on the Gandhi Setu, which connects Patna to Hajipur in Vaishali district. During his visit on 21 November, the Prime Minister will also inaugurate and lay foundation stones for several development projects at a public meeting at Rajapakar in Vaishali district. The bridge, built as an extradosed cable-stayed structure, will allow speeds of up to 100 km per hour. Frequently Asked Questions What is Nitish Setu? bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar to set up 44 hi-tech sugarcane nurseries with subsidy of up to Rs 11.25 lakh each
bihar_raw_news.content: All News English Indian Sugar News Sugar News Bihar is planning to establish 44 hi-tech sugarcane nurseries to promote cultivation and ensure the availability of quality, disease-free planting material to farmers across the state, Amar Ujala reported. The Sugarcane Industries Department has introduced the scheme for the first time, with a target of producing around 2.20 crore improved and disease-free sugarcane seedlings annually through the proposed nurseries. Each nursery is expected to produce around five lakh seedlings a year using the single-bud plantlet technique. Work is progressing at four locations. One nursery is being established in Patna district and another in Jamui, while two more have been approved in Muzaffarpur district. Bihar currently has around 2.25 lakh hectares under sugarcane cultivation. The department aims to expand cultivation, particularly in areas that are not served by sugar mills. The availability of quality planting material is also expected to support the proposed establishment of 25 new sugar mills and the revival of closed mills, which will require a reliable supply of sugarcane. The scheme also aims to increase farmers’ income through local nursery operations and create employment opportunities for rural youth and women. The nurseries will be developed under a public-private partnership model. Progressive farmers, JEEViKA groups, farmer-producer organisations, self-help groups, private entrepreneurs, sugar mills and jaggery manufacturers are eligible to apply through the Bihar Cane Care portal. The estimated cost of setting up one nursery is Rs 15 lakh, taking the total cost for 44 nurseries to Rs 6.60 crore. The government will provide a subsidy of up to 75% of the project cost, subject to a maximum of Rs 11.25 lakh per nursery.

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Museum beats the Louvre in Global Museum Rankings; Here's what makes it stand out
bihar_raw_news.content: Compiled By : Salma Sulthana Last Updated: 14 November 2026, 02:56 PM IST 5 min Share Follow us on Ranked ninth among the world's best museums in 2026, Bihar Museum in Patna offers ancient sculptures, Mithila art, historical treasures and contemporary exhibitions ❎ If the Louvre in Paris or the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York is on your travel wish list, there is another museum you might want to visit before. The Bihar Museum ranked ninth on German travel guide Worth a Journey’s 2026 list of the world's 100 best museums. It stands one place above New York's famous Met, while the Louvre features at number 31. The ranking makes it the highest-placed museum in Asia and the only Indian institution on the list. To advertise here, Contact Us But the reason to make a trip here goes beyond its position on a global list. Spread across nearly 14 acres, the museum brings together archaeological treasures, ancient sculptures, regional art traditions and contemporary works. It offers a chance to explore Bihar's history and its influence on India's cultural landscape, all under one roof. Why Bihar deserves a place on your museum itinerary The museum's story began with a space problem. Patna Museum, established in 1917, had accumulated around 40,000 artefacts, but its galleries could display only a small part of the collection. The proposal to add more space eventually gave way to a much bigger idea: creating a modern museum that could present Bihar's history and artistic heritage to a wider audience. The result is the Bihar Museum, a 13.9-acre complex designed by Japanese architectural firm Maki and Associates in collaboration with Mumbai-based OPOLIS. Construction began in 2013, and the museum opened its first sections to visitors in August 2015. The remaining galleries followed in October 2017. The architecture is worth noticing before you even enter the galleries. Rather than one imposing block, the museum follows a campus-style layout, with different sections connected through walkways and open spaces. Weathering steel, stone, terracotta and glass give the buildings a contemporary appearance while drawing on materials associated with the region's history. What should you look out for inside? With more than 20,000 artefacts listed in its collection, the museum takes visitors through different periods of Bihar's history, from prehistoric times and ancient kingdoms to later cultural influences. The galleries are arranged thematically and chronologically, so there is plenty to explore even if you are not someone who usually spends an afternoon in a museum. Here are some of the sections worth making time for. The Didarganj Yakshi: If there is one exhibit you should not leave without seeing, it is this sculpture. Standing 5 feet 2 inches tall, the female figure is carved from Chunar sandstone and dates to the third century BCE. It was discovered on the banks of the Ganga at Didarganj, Patna, in 1917. bihar_raw_news.title: Mob vandalises Bihar hospital, sets ambulance ablaze after dispute turns violent
bihar_raw_news.content: Mob vandalises Bihar hospital, sets ambulance ablaze after dispute turns violent Written By : Medical Dialogues Team Published On 2026-11-14T12:44:22+05:30 | Updated On 14 Nov 2026 2:45 PM IST Aurangabad: In a shocking incident, an ambulance was set on fire, and a private hospital in Bihar's Aurangabad district was vandalised after a dispute over the treatment of a patient escalated into violence on Thursday. The incident led to a major law-and-order situation, with an angry mob also blocking a main road for nearly five hours. According to reports, the dispute reportedly began on Tuesday night after a disagreement arose over the treatment of a female patient suffering from severe anaemia. The hospital had advised shifting the patient to another facility, but a relative of another patient objected, saying he would arrange blood for her instead. The disagreement between the doctor and the patient's relative subsequently turned into a physical altercation. During the dispute, a 45-year-old man from Charkupa village was allegedly assaulted and sustained serious injuries . He was subsequently shifted to Patna for further treatment. His condition reportedly deteriorated on Thursday, and he went into a coma. News of his deteriorating condition reached nearby villages, triggering anger among his relatives and local residents. Also Read:Hospital staff attacked, property vandalised over treatment charges in Nagpur Tension escalated further after rumours circulated that the injured man had died. A large crowd gathered outside the private hospital and allegedly damaged the clinic premises. An ambulance was set on fire, while furniture and other items inside the facility were vandalised . The protesters also blocked the RafiGanj-Gaya main road, disrupting traffic for around five hours, Dainik Bhaskar reported. Fire brigade personnel who arrived to control the blaze reportedly faced opposition from the mob, forcing them to deal with the situation amid heightened tension. Senior police and administrative officials, along with additional security personnel, reached the spot and attempted to pacify the protesters. The road blockade was eventually lifted after several rounds of discussions between the administration and local representatives. Police said the doctor and the compounder had been taken into custody and that an investigation into the incident was underway. Authorities have maintained a watch in the area to prevent further unrest. The incident has raised concerns over the escalation of disputes inside healthcare facilities and the safety of medical staff, patients and hospital property during such confrontations. bihar_raw_news.title: Two Bihar boys rescued from bonded labour in Odisha receive first rehabilitation aid a year later
bihar_raw_news.content: The boys were allegedly made to work from 5 am to 10 pm without wages. Express Illustration Odisha Two Bihar boys rescued from bonded labour in Odisha receive first rehabilitation aid a year later The 12- and 14-year-olds, allegedly forced to work up to 17 hours a day at gupchup-making units in Ganjam, received Rs 30,000 each in October, against an entitlement of Rs 2 lakh apiece. Sisir Panigrahy Updated: 14th Nov, 2026 at 10:36 AM BERHAMPUR: For two young boys brought from Bihar to work in gupchup-making units in Ganjam’s Hinjilicut, being rescued from exploitation did not mean an immediate return of their childhood. Although they were freed in October 2025, their first instalment of rehabilitation assistance of Rs 30,000 each was released on October 23, 2026, nearly a year after their rescue. The boys, aged 12 and 14, are to get Rs 2 lakh each. The boys were allegedly made to work from 5 am to 10 pm without wages. They were reportedly beaten if they failed to meet sales targets and prevented from attending school or communicating with their families. Their parents were allegedly promised monthly wages and given advances of Rs 3,000 and Rs 5,000, respectively. On the eve of Children’s Day, their case highlights a larger concern in Odisha, where poverty and advance payments to parents can push children into conditions of bondage, while inadequate identification of such cases may deprive them of protection under the Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act. Bonded child labour is not always recognised as distinct from ordinary child labour. If officials treat such cases only under general child labour provisions, children may miss the release and rehabilitation benefits available under the bonded labour legislation. Add as a preferred source on Google A case in Ganjam’s Chikiti block illustrates this gap. A boy was allegedly forced to graze buffaloes for nearly two years without wages and kept almost like a prisoner. He was rescued on September 1, 2026, and was declared a freed bonded labourer on September 10, making him eligible for rehabilitation assistance. However, after the child welfare committee handed him over to his parents, the employer allegedly took him away again. His parents reportedly alleged that the employer threatened them and demanded repayment of the money he claimed to have advanced to them. The boy was rescued a second time only after a police case was registered. Jajpur has demonstrated rehabilitation assistance can be delivered under the revised Rehabilitation of Bonded Labourer Scheme-2026. In September, it became the first district in Odisha to disburse assistance under the scheme. Eight children rescued during 2024-25 received financial assistance of Rs 40,000 each. Incidentally, two children were rescued from bonded labour in Jajpur on Friday. bihar_raw_news.title: Tigers to Be Relocated to Buxa Tiger Reserve from Assam and Bihar - Drishti IAS
bihar_raw_news.content: West Bengal Prev Next Tigers to Be Relocated to Buxa Tiger Reserve from Assam and Bihar 14 Nov 2026 5 min read Why in News? West Bengal has announced plans to relocate two more tigers from Assam and Bihar to Buxa Tiger Reserve (BTR) by the end of November 2026. The initiative aims to strengthen the reserve's resident tiger population as part of a phased tiger reintroduction and recovery programme. Key Points: Proposed Tiger Relocation Destination: Buxa Tiger Reserve, Alipurduar district, West Bengal. Source states: Assam and Bihar. Number of tigers: Two. Expected timeline: By the end of November 2026. Objective: To strengthen the resident tiger population and establish a viable, breeding and self-sustaining tiger population in Buxa. The relocation programme is being undertaken under the supervision of the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) . Earlier Relocation of a Tigress from Bihar On 2 October 2026 , a three-year-old tigress, identified as T138 , was released into Buxa Tiger Reserve. It was translocated from Valmiki Tiger Reserve, Bihar , marking the beginning of the phased tiger reintroduction programme. The tigress subsequently moved into Assam and was captured by forest personnel using a tranquilliser dart. It was brought back to Buxa on 4 November 2026 . Tiger Augmentation and Recovery Programme The tiger recovery initiative in Buxa has been implemented by the West Bengal Government with support from the NTCA and the Wildlife Institute of India (WII) . The collaborative recovery project has been underway since 2018 . Major interventions include: Prey-base augmentation: More than 800 chital have been released to improve prey availability. Habitat restoration: Approximately 380 hectares of grassland have been restored or converted over the past eight years. Scientific monitoring: Camera traps and telemetry are used to monitor tiger movement and population recovery. Protection measures: Strengthening anti-poaching activities and forest protection. Community participation: Engagement of 64 Eco-Development Committees and Joint Forest Management Committees. The programme aims to complement natural tiger recovery through scientifically guided interventions. Why Buxa Tiger Reserve Was Selected for Tiger Reintroduction Buxa experienced a prolonged absence of a stable resident tiger population due to: Habitat degradation and fragmentation. Changes in land use. Decline in prey availability. Increasing anthropogenic pressure. The reserve has ecological connectivity with Bhutan and adjoining forest landscapes of Assam . Camera-trap evidence has indicated natural tiger movement through the wider landscape, including an individual matched with a tiger from Manas Tiger Reserve, Assam , in 2023. About Buxa Tiger Reserve Location: Alipurduar district, West Bengal. Established as a Tiger Reserve: 1983, under Project Tiger. Area: Approximately 760.87 sq. km. Geographical significance: Located in the eastern Himalayan foothills and the Dooars region. Ecological connectivity: Linked with forest landscapes of Bhutan and Assam. Major rivers: Sankosh, Raidak, Jayanti and Torsa are associated with the wider landscape. Vegetation: Tropical moist and dry deciduous forests, along with other forest types. Important wildlife: Bengal tiger, Asian elephant, leopard, gaur and several other species. About Project Tiger Launch: 1 April 1973. Nodal Ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and

bihar_raw_news.title: Nitish Setu Inauguration Gets 35-Official Push Ahead of Modi Visit - Urban Acres
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News Nitish Setu Inauguration Gets 35-Official Push Ahead of Modi Visit Breaking News Nitish Setu Inauguration Gets 35-Official Push Ahead of Modi Visit By Maria Dsouza November 14, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Preparations for the inauguration of the six-lane Kachchi Dargah-Bidupur bridge, named Nitish Setu, have intensified ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s scheduled visit to Vaishali on November 21, with the Bihar government deploying 35 senior officials and the NDA organising booth-level mobilisation for the programme. Modi is scheduled to inaugurate the Jandaha-Rajapakar industrial area and formally dedicate the bridge across the Ganga to the public during the visit. The state government has named the bridge Nitish Setu. The general administration department has deputed the 35 senior officials to oversee arrangements and coordinate between departments. They will be stationed in Vaishali from November 17 until the conclusion of the Prime Minister’s visit. The deployment is intended to ensure that preparations are completed on time and that the programme is conducted smoothly, according to the report. A review meeting was held at Jafarpatti in Rajapakar block to assess the progress of preparations. Deputy Chief Minister Bijendra Prasad Yadav, BJP state president Sanjay Saraogi and JD(U) state president Umesh Singh Kushwaha attended the meeting and inspected the venue. Officials briefed the leaders on the arrangements and were directed to complete the remaining work within the stipulated timeframe. The bridge is among the key infrastructure projects linked to the visit. The Kachchi Dargah-Bidupur crossing is a six-lane structure over the Ganga, connecting the Patna-side Kachchi Dargah area with Bidupur in Vaishali district. Its formal opening is expected to add a major river-crossing link to the region’s road network, although the report does not provide details of traffic operations, tolling, access roads or the project’s construction cost. The Jandaha-Rajapakar industrial area is also scheduled to be inaugurated. The report does not specify its total area, investment commitments, industries planned or the number of jobs expected. Both projects are being presented as part of a wider set of development initiatives and projects that the Prime Minister is expected to unveil for Bihar during the visit. Alongside the administrative preparations, NDA constituents met at the JD(U) state headquarters to coordinate the political mobilisation. The meeting was attended by Umesh Singh Kushwaha, Sanjay Saraogi, LJP (Ram Vilas) state president Surendra Vivek, HAM-S state president Anil Kumar and RLM acting state president Prashant Pankaj. The alliance leaders discussed booth-level coordination, mutual understanding among the constituent parties and the management of workers for the programme. They also thanked Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary for naming the bridge after former chief minister and JD(U) president Nitish Kumar, describing the proposed inauguration as a matter of pride and joy for Bihar. The immediate administrative milestone is the deployment of the 35 senior officials in Vaishali from November 17. Preparations will continue until the Prime Minister’s scheduled visit and the proposed inauguration of Nitish Setu and the Jandaha-Rajapakar industrial area on November 21. Share Copy URL

national_raw_news.title: Govt announces 5 lakh pucca houses for poor families in Odisha under PMAY-Gramin
national_raw_news.content: Union Minister for Rural Development Shivraj Singh Chouhan today announced five lakh pucca houses for poor families in Odisha under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Gramin. Mr Chouhan announced this while addressing a state-level program of the scheme in Balangir in the presence of Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi. The Union Minister said that a fresh and proper survey had now been completed and no poor family would be left living in a kutcha house. He said, all eligible families would receive pucca houses in a phased manner. He also announced that the Centre and the state government would jointly provide subsidies for installing solar panels on houses. He said, this would help beneficiaries bring their electricity bills down to zero and earn additional income by selling surplus electricity. Mr Chouhan appreciated Odisha for achieving the target of 27 lakh Lakhpati Didis a year ahead of schedule, with 29 lakh women now having attained this status. Mr Chouhan said that over the next five years, loans worth 10 lakh crore rupees would be extended through banks to women across the country to help more women become Lakhpati Didis. He added that access to credit would no longer be limited to members of self-help groups. He added that women who wish to start their own businesses or livelihood activities individually would also be able to obtain loans without the requirement of a guarantee. Outlining the government’s plans for rural development, Mr Chouhan said Odisha would receive approximately four thousand crore rupees this year under the Viksit Bharat-G RAM G scheme. This would provide every panchayat with 25 lakh to 50 lakh rupees annually. He said, over five years, smaller panchayats would receive up to one crore rupees e and larger panchayats up to two crore rupees for development works. Mr Chouhan who is also the Minister of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare Minister assured that the new agriculture college in Balangir would be developed into the country’s finest agricultural institution.

national_raw_news.title: PM Modi to participate in Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas programme in Maharashtra tomorrow
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will participate in the Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas programme in Gadchiroli, Maharashtra tomorrow via video conferencing. The Programme marks the 151st Birth Anniversary of Dharti Aaba Bhagwan Birsa Munda. He will also address the gathering on the occasion. During the programme, the Prime Minister will inaugurate and lay the foundation stone of 246 development projects worth around three thousand crore rupees. These projects are aimed at strengthening education, healthcare, livelihoods and community infrastructure for tribal communities across the country. Besides, Mr Modi will also inaugurate 173 projects, including 38 Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS) for tribal students and 100 Multi-Purpose Centres. These projects come under the Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN), which will serve as hubs for service delivery and community activities. The Prime Minister will lay the foundation stone of 19 new Eklavya Model Residential Schools and 12 Tribal Multipurpose Marketing Centres (TMMCs). He will also inaugurate various other projects under PM-JANMAN and the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA). In addition, the Prime Minister will also lay the foundation stone for 42 other projects under PM-JANMAN and DAJGUA. Mr Modi will also inaugurate Tribal Research Institute (TRI) building at Itanagar, Arunachal Pradesh and Ropuiliani Tribal Freedom Fighter Museum in Mizoram, aimed at preserving tribal culture and heritage. The programme will mark the culmination of Janjatiya Gaurav Pakhwada, being observed across the country from 1st to 15th of this month.

national_raw_news.title: Railways approve weekly train service between Nepal and India for convenience of pilgrims & ...
national_raw_news.content: Indian Railways has approved the introduction of a new weekly train service between Janakpur Dham in Nepal and Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh, India. This weekly service will connect Janakpur Dham with Ayodhya Cantt., passing through several important towns and cities in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh. It will cover a distance of nearly 604 kilometres. Ministry of Railways said that the train service will operate once a week, with its originating days being Saturday from Janakpur Dham and Monday from Ayodhya Cantt. The train will have commercial stoppages at Jaynagar, Madhubani, Shisho, Sitamarhi, Raxaul, Narkatiaganj, Gorakhpur, Basti, Mankapur and Ayodhya Dham, besides its terminal stations. The new train service is expected to make cross-border travel more convenient for pilgrims, tourists and other passengers. It will facilitate religious journeys between Janakpur and Ayodhya, encourage tourism circuits associated with the Ramayana and provide greater mobility to people travelling for education, business and family-related purposes. India and Nepal share centuries-old cultural, historical and social bonds, with religious traditions and cross-border community relationships forming an integral part of this partnership. The new train service will add another dimension to bilateral cooperation by using railway connectivity to bring communities closer. The Ministry said that the initiative is a signigicant step towards strengthening cross-border connectivity, religious tourism and India-Nepal Friendship.

national_raw_news.title: Men’s U-19 Asia Cup: India defeat Pakistan to clinch title for ninth time 3 hours ago 309
national_raw_news.content: In Men’s Cricket, India defeated Pakistan by one wicket in a thrilling final to clinch the Men’s Under-19 Asia Cup title in Muscat, Oman, today. Lower-order batters Manal Chauhan and Mohit Ulva played sensational knocks to help India snatch victory from the jaws of defeat and successfully chase down a challenging target of 338 runs. Needing three runs off the final delivery, Mohit Ulva struck a boundary to seal India’s record-extending ninth title. Mohit remained unbeaten on 49 off just 26 deliveries, while Manal Chauhan contributed a valuable 47 off 32 balls. Skipper Lakshya Raichandani also played a crucial role with a brilliant 80-run knock. Mohit Ulva was named player of the match, while Aaryavir Sehwag was awarded player of the tournament. Earlier, opting to bat first, Pakistan posted 337 for 9 in their allotted 50 overs. Their innings was powered by a century from Usman Khan and half-centuries from Abdul Qadir and Farhan Yousaf. For India, Kavya Patel led India’s bowling attack, claiming four wickets. President Droupadi Murmu congratulated Team India on winning the Men’s Under-19 Asia Cup. In a social media post, the President lauded the young champions for displaying exceptional skill, determination, and composure throughout the closely contested final match. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has also congratulated the young cricketers. In a social media post, Mr Modi said that today is an outstanding day for Indian cricket. He said that their success will inspire several youngsters. Congratulating young cricketers, Union Home Minister Amit Shah said that the determination, firm resolve, and excellent sportsmanship they demonstrated on the pitch were a masterclass in India’s cricketing excellence.

national_raw_news.title: 21 films from BRICS countries to be featured at IFFI 2026 2 hours ago 30
national_raw_news.content: The 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026, to be held in Goa from 20th to 28th of this month, will feature a special showcase of 21 films from BRICS countries under the section ‘Films from BRICS’. The curated section, bringing stories of struggle, identity, history and social change from across the world to the big screen, explores themes such as democracy, freedom, colonialism, social inequality, displacement, family and belonging. Rooted in the histories and contemporary realities of their respective societies, the films offer audiences insights into diverse cultures and shared human experiences. The selection includes films from Brazil, Indonesia, South Africa, China, Iran, Saudi Arabia, Nigeria and several other countries. India’s entry in the section is ‘Article 370’, directed by Aditya Dhar. Set against the backdrop of the 2016 Kashmir unrest, the film follows a mission to abrogate Article 370. It received three honours at the 72nd National Film Awards in the categories of Best Film, Best Actress and Best Music. Among the other notable entries, Brazil’s ‘Amadeo and the Hypothetical New World’ explores the struggle against slavery, while Indonesia’s ‘The Sea Speaks His Name’ revisits the country’s 1998 pro-democracy movement through the story of a missing student activist and his family’s search for answers. South Africa’s ‘The Trek’ is set in the Kalahari Desert in the mid-19th century and highlights the harsh realities of the colonial era. Contemporary concerns also feature prominently in the selection. ‘Dreaming of Serenada’, a Uganda-UK documentary, explores climate change and its impact on communities through a father-daughter relationship. Ethiopia-US production ‘Faya Dayi’ examines the lives and aspirations of communities associated with khat cultivation and consumption. Scheduled from 20th to 28th of this month across multiple venues in Goa, the 57th IFFI will showcase over 150 international films from 86 countries. The festival will bring together films across genres, countries and languages through its competitive and non-competitive sections, curated packages, retrospectives, tributes and thematic showcases, providing a platform for cross-cultural exchange and cinematic excellence.

national_raw_news.title: Hockey player Lalremsiami Hmar becomes first sportperson from Mizoram to receive Arjuna award 13 Nov 2026 | 5:04 PM 482
national_raw_news.content: Indian women’s hockey player and Olympian Lalremsiami Hmar today became the first sportsperson from Mizoram to receive the prestigious Arjuna Award, adding another milestone to her trailblazing career. The 26-year-old was among 17 sportspersons selected for the Arjuna Award 2025 by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports on August 18. President Droupadi Murmu formally presented the honour to her at a ceremony at Rashtrapati Bhavan in New Delhi today. Lalremsiami, who hailed from Kolasib in the northern part of Mizoram bordering Assam, took up hockey at a young age. Her talent was spotted by teachers Lallawmawmi, Lalrampari and Lalrothuami, who encouraged her to pursue the sport. Lalremsiami joined the state-run hockey academy at Thenzawl in 2011 at the age of 11, before moving to the National Hockey Academy in New Delhi in 2016. Lalremsiami made her national debut at the Junior Nehru Hockey Tournament in October 2011 and was later selected for India’s Under-18 team for the Asian Cup in 2016. She earned her first senior national team call-up in 2017 and was part of India’s Asia Cup-winning side that year. Since then, she has established herself as a key member of the Indian team, featuring in several major international tournaments, including the Tokyo Olympics 2020, where India finished fourth. She created history in 2018 by becoming the first sportsperson from Mizoram to win an Asian Games medal, helping India secure silver. Her commitment to the national team drew widespread admiration in 2019 when she chose to remain with the squad for the FIH Women’s Series in Japan despite the death of her father, Lalthansanga Zote. India won the tournament and secured qualification for the Tokyo Olympics, making Lalremsiami the first woman from Mizoram to compete at the Olympics. She followed in the footsteps of archer C. Lalremsanga, who represented India at the 1992 Barcelona and 1996 Atlanta Olympics. In 2020, Lalremsiami became the first Indian female hockey player to win the International Hockey Federation’s Women’s Rising Star of the Year award. Her list of achievements has since grown to include a bronze at the 2022 Asian Games, Asian Champions Trophy titles in 2023 and 2024, and gold at the 2026 Asian Games. The Mizoram government had earlier announced a cash reward of Rs 40 lakh each for Lalremsiami and fellow Mizo player Lalthantluangi for their contribution to India’s women’s hockey team that won gold at the Asian Games on October 2. The Arjuna Award now adds another distinction to Lalremsiami’s career, making her the first sportsperson from Mizoram to receive one of the country’s highest honours for sporting achievement.

national_raw_news.title: Low-Pressure Area over Southeast Bay of Bengal likely to intensify into depression: IMD 2 hours ago 38
national_raw_news.content: India Meteorological Department (IMD) has said that a well-marked Low-Pressure Area has formed over Southeast Bay of Bengal today. It is very likely to move northwestwards and intensify into a depression over the same region during next 24 Hours. Thereafter, it is likely to move north-northwestwards and intensify further into a cyclonic storm over the central parts of south and adjoining west central Bay of Bengal around Monday evening. IMD has advised the fishermen out at sea to return to coasts by tomorrow. It also cautioned fishermen not to venture into Andaman Sea and along and off Andaman and Nicobar Islands till Monday. The Met Department has forecast heavy rainfall over Andaman and Nicobar Islands till Monday. According to IMD, thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty winds are likely to prevail over Rajasthan and Uttarakhand tomorrow. The Weather Agency has said that a western disturbance is likely to cause light or moderate rainfall or snowfall over Western Himalayan Region and light rainfall over plains of Northwest India on tomorrow. Dense Fog is very likely at isolated places over West Uttar Pradesh tomorrow. Meanwhile, air quality in Delhi-NCR is in the Very Poor category. According to the Central Pollution Control Board, Delhi’s Air Quality Index (AQI) was recorded at 367 as of 8 PM today.

national_raw_news.title: US resumes flight operations after telecommunications failure disrupted air traffic control natio...
national_raw_news.content: The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) today temporarily halted departing flights across the country following a telecommunications failure that affected air traffic control centres, disrupting thousands of flights across the country. According to flight-tracking services, nearly 7,000 flights were delayed or cancelled following the ground stop. The FAA said the communications outage affected all 22 Air Route Traffic Control Centres across the United States, prompting the suspension of departures as a precautionary measure. Later, the US authorities lifted the nationwide ground stop that disrupted thousands of flights and stranded passengers across the country, clearing the way for airlines to resume operations after more than four hours. Meanwhile, US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said, FAA technicians are investigating the communications failure. Aircraft already in the air were allowed to land, while departing flights were temporarily suspended. The disruption initially affected air traffic control operations in Chicago before the FAA extended the restrictions nationwide. US Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was no indication that the incident was linked to a security threat or deliberate attack. He assured the public that passengers were safe and all aircraft had been accounted for, while cautioning that restoring normal operations could take time. Mr Mullin said authorities were examining all possible causes of the telecommunications failure, including a potential connection with the planned introduction of a new artificial intelligence tool designed to assist air traffic controllers. He also confirmed that President Donald Trump has been briefed on the situation. The incident marks the second nationwide suspension of US flight departures since the terrorist attack on 11th of September in 2001.

national_raw_news.title: PM Modi says India moving towards global leadership in emerging technologies
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said India is moving towards global leadership in emerging technologies, from chips to ships, and from Artificial Intelligence and data centres to quantum computing. He emphasised that reliable power generation is essential to achieving this ambition. Mr Modi said the country is expanding its nuclear power capacity as part of its efforts to achieve clean energy goals and meet its growing energy requirements. The Prime Minister was addressing the gathering at Bengaluru in Karnataka yesterday, after launching development projects worth over 15,600 crore rupees. Mr Modi said the projects, covering metro, railways and energy infrastructure, will strengthen connectivity, boost economic growth and create new employment opportunities in the state. Prime Minister Modi highlighted the importance of energy security in view of the ongoing conflict in the Iran and Gulf region. He said India strengthened its energy infrastructure over the past decade by expanding fuel production and storage capacity, along with investments in solar, hydro and wind energy. He said India’s renewable energy capacity had crossed 300 gigawatts. Pointing out that Central schemes are transforming Indian citizens from electricity consumers into electricity producers, he also highlighted the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana and PM-KUSUM scheme, saying these initiatives are helping households and farmers become producers of clean energy. The Prime Minister also outlined three major energy projects in Karnataka. These include the Mangaluru LPG project, which will add 80,000 metric tonnes of storage capacity; the Devangonthi Marketing Terminal, aimed at streamlining the supply of petrol, diesel and aviation fuel; and a compressed biogas plant in Bengaluru, with a production capacity of 13 tonnes per day. Mr Modi said the biogas plant will improve waste management and help reduce expenditure on natural gas imports. Describing Bengaluru as India’s Silicon Valley, Prime Minister Modi said the city contributes more than one-third of the country’s IT exports and serves as a major centre of innovation and economic growth. He noted that the Namma Metro network has expanded from just 17 kilometres in 2014 to over 100 kilometres today, making Bengaluru the third city in the country, after Delhi-NCR and the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, to achieve this milestone. He said the newly inaugurated Pink Line of Bengaluru Metro will improve connectivity to educational institutions, including IIM Bengaluru, as well as major business and technology hubs. The Prime Minister also highlighted railway modernisation, including the development of Amrit Bharat stations and the expansion of Vande Bharat services. He also flagged off a new Vande Bharat train connecting Karnataka with Goa, following the recent introduction of the state’s first Vande Bharat Sleeper train. He said the new service would improve connectivity along Karnataka’s coastal region, including Mangaluru, and offer passengers a faster and more comfortable travel experience.

national_raw_news.title: Environment Minister assesses measures to mitigate air pollution in Delhi-NCR 21 mins ago 6
national_raw_news.content: Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Bhupender Yadav, today chaired a review meeting to assess measures undertaken by Delhi, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan for mitigation of air pollution in Delhi-NCR. During the meeting, the Minister directed all agencies to move beyond planning and ensure rigorous, time-bound and coordinated enforcement on the ground. Emphasising that air pollution does not recognise State boundaries, he called for coordinated implementation of matching pollution control measures across NCR. Mr Yadav also stressed real-time monitoring through Integrated Command and Control Centres and direct accountability of field officers for violations. Furthermore, State Governments were directed to nominate Secretary level officials for 7 cities in Haryana, 4 cities in UP and 4 cities in Rajasthan for making them responsible for implementation of pollution control measures through field visits and report to CAQM on weekly basis. In the meeting CAQM was requested to issue notices to non-performing officers. Meanwhile the CPCB was directed to immediately seal the identified 191 non-conforming polluting industries, which despite repeated directions had not even placed orders for installation of Air Pollution Control Devices. Concluding the review, Mr Yadav emphasised that coordinated efforts, field-level accountability and visible action on the ground are essential to effectively address the challenge of air pollution in Delhi-NCR. The meeting held today was attended by Delhi Environment Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa, Haryana Environment Minister Rao Narbir Singh and UP Environment Minister Arun Kumar Saxena virtually. The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change said that Mr Yadav has held more than 30 review meetings with NCR State Governments, Municipal Bodies over the past one year. It added that these meetings are aimed at strengthening air pollution preparedness and ensuring effective implementation of control measures.

national_raw_news.title: Indian markets continue winning streak for third consecutive week due to strong FII inflows 1 hour ago 735
national_raw_news.content: Indian stock market extended its gaining streak for the third consecutive week, supported by strong foreign institutional investor (FII) inflows and better-than-expected corporate earnings. However, rising retail inflation, elevated US Treasury yields, rupee weakness and uncertainty surrounding the global monetary policy outlook limit the pace of gains. The 30-share Sensex at the Bombay Stock Exchange climbed 564 points, or 0.7 per cent, to close at 81 thousand 592. The National Stock Exchange Nifty 50 gained 114 points, or nearly half a per cent to end at 25 thousand and 144. In the broader market on the National Stock Exchange, Midcap 100 index soared 2.1 per cent, while the Smallcap 100 index surged 3.6 per cent during the week. On the sectoral front, the Nifty PSU Bank index emerged as the top performer, surging 7.5 per cent over the week. The Nifty Media index advanced 5.2 per cent, while the Nifty Capital Markets index gained 3.8 per cent. In contrast, the Nifty IT index was the weakest performer among the major sectoral indices, declining 3.2 per cent, while the Nifty Cement index slipped 2.1 per cent. Investor wealth on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) witnessed a significant uptick this week, with the combined market capitalisation of all listed companies surging by over 7 lakh crore rupees. In the forex market, the Indian rupee depreciated by 34 paise this week to settle at 94 rupees and 25 paise against the US dollar.

national_raw_news.title: India records all-time high exports of nearly 90 billion dollars in October: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal 9 hours ago 267
national_raw_news.content: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has said, India recorded an all-time high in exports, reaching nearly 90 billion dollars in October this year. Addressing the inaugural ceremony of the India International Trade Fair (IITF) in New Delhi yesterday, Mr Goyal said the export figure of October comprised around 50 billion dollars in merchandise exports and 40 billion dollars in services exports. He further informed that India’s cumulative exports during the first seven months of the current financial year, up to October, has reached 570 billion dollars. Expressing confidence in the country’s export performance, the Minister said India is well on course to achieve its one-trillion-dollar export target this year. Mr Goyal also expressed confidence that India’s international trade will register growth of 15 to 16 per cent during the current year, despite ongoing conflicts and global uncertainties. He said the country’s performance reflects the resilience of its economy, the confidence of its exporters and India’s ability to overcome global challenges with determination and self-respect. Highlighting the strength of India’s domestic economy, Mr Goyal referred to the strong business activity witnessed during the recent festive season, particularly around Diwali. He said markets across the country recorded robust consumer demand and increased business activity. The Minister also pointed out that GST collections in October touched an all-time high for the month. He expressed confidence that November would also see record collections, reflecting the continued momentum of economic activity across the country. Referring to India’s long-term economic ambitions, Mr Goyal said the country, currently a four-trillion-dollar economy, aspires to become a 30-trillion-dollar economy by 2047. Speaking about the India International Trade Fair, the Minister said, the event has emerged as an important platform bringing together states, businesses, products and India’s diverse capabilities under one roof. He announced that the India Trade Promotion Organisation would take the IITF platform to international destinations by organising several overseas trade fairs, covering both specific sectors and multiple industries. These initiatives will provide Indian manufacturers, service providers and start-ups with opportunities to showcase their capabilities and connect with buyers and markets across the world, including developed economies. Mr Goyal added that the 45th edition of IITF had moved beyond incremental improvements, marking a significant step towards the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047. The annual India International Trade Fair, organised by the India Trade Promotion Organisation, begins in New Delhi today. It brings together more than 3,500 exhibitors from India and abroad. The theme of this year’s fair is ‘Vikas aur Virasat’. A total of 32 States and Union Territories will participate in the 14-day event, showcasing their regional products, local industries, traditional crafts, cultural heritage, tourism potential and development initiatives. The fair will provide a major platform for businesses, entrepreneurs and participating states to promote their products, explore new opportunities and strengthen domestic as well as international trade ties.

national_raw_news.title: National Tribal Cultural Festival ‘Bhagwan Birsa Kala Sangam 2.0’ begins in Maharashtra’s Gadchiroli 2 hours ago 32
national_raw_news.content: In Maharashtra, the National Tribal Cultural Festival, ‘Bhagwan Birsa Kala Sangam 2.0’, is being celebrated in Gadchiroli from today, marking the 151st birth anniversary of legendary tribal freedom fighter Bhagwan Birsa Munda. The Tribal Development Department of the Maharashtra Government is organising this special cultural festival to celebrate the rich heritage, traditions and artistic legacy of tribal communities. Union Tribal Affairs Minister Jual Oram attended the inaugural function as the Chief Guest, while State Tribal Development Minister Dr Ashok Uike inaugurated the programme. Addressing the gathering, Mr Oram said that Gadchiroli, once known as a Naxal-affected district, has now become Naxal-free due to the sustained efforts of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah. He said this transformation was one of the reasons why Gadchiroli was chosen to host the main national celebration of Janjatiya Gaurav Divas. The festival showcases the vibrant cultural diversity of tribal communities through traditional dances, folk songs, musical performances, handicrafts, paintings and digital art. Special exhibitions on tribal religious and cultural traditions, along with theatrical presentations depicting the valour and sacrifices of great tribal heroes, are also among the major attractions. The event provides a national platform for tribal artists, students and young performers to showcase their talent while promoting awareness about the rich cultural heritage of tribal communities. Meanwhile, Prime Minister Narendra Modi will address the main programme of the sixth Janjatiya Gaurav Divas in Gadchiroli tomorrow through video conferencing. The Governor of Maharashtra, the Chief Minister and Union Ministers will attend the national-level celebrations.

national_raw_news.title: No Compromise on Devotees’ Safety: CM Yogi Directs Officials to Ensure Elaborate Chhath Arrangements
national_raw_news.content: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Friday directed officials to ensure comprehensive arrangements for the safety, convenience and cleanliness of devotees during Chhath Mahaparva, stressing that there would be no compromise on public safety and essential facilities at ghats across the state. Chairing a high-level review meeting through video conferencing, the Chief Minister instructed district administrations to complete all preparations well in advance, particularly in districts expected to witness large gatherings, including Varanasi, Gorakhpur, Ballia, Azamgarh, Ghazipur, Lucknow, Ghaziabad, Basti and Kanpur Nagar. Describing Chhath as a festival rooted in faith, discipline, purity and gratitude towards nature, Adityanath said lakhs of devotees would participate in the celebrations across the state. He noted that devotees would offer arghya to the setting Sun on the evening of November 15, while the four-day festival would conclude on November 16 with prayers and offerings to the rising Sun. The Chief Minister directed officials to inspect all major ghats, rivers, ponds and other water bodies and ensure proper cleaning, adequate lighting, accessible approach roads, drinking water facilities, toilets and changing rooms for women. Emphasising devotees’ safety, he ordered the installation of strong barricades and warning signboards at vulnerable locations after assessing water levels and depths. Adequate numbers of trained divers, boats and water police personnel must be deployed to prevent accidents, while CCTV cameras and public address systems should be installed for surveillance and crowd management, he said. Adityanath also called for special arrangements for women, children and senior citizens, directing authorities to deploy sufficient police personnel, including women officers, at major ghats. He asked police personnel to discharge their duties with restraint, sensitivity and a cooperative approach. District-level control rooms and effective coordination between police and administrative officials should also be ensured, he added. The Chief Minister directed officials to prepare traffic management plans, identify necessary diversions and designate parking areas in advance to prevent congestion around puja sites. In view of the festival-related travel rush, Adityanath instructed the Uttar Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation to operate additional buses from Delhi to various districts of eastern Uttar Pradesh. He also directed officials to ensure that passengers were not charged fares above the prescribed rates. The Urban Development and Panchayati Raj departments were asked to organise special cleanliness drives around ghats and ensure uninterrupted power supply, with alternative lighting arrangements wherever necessary. The Chief Minister further directed authorities to ensure the availability of first-aid camps, ambulances and emergency services at major puja sites. Warning against negligence, Adityanath reiterated that cleanliness, safety and public convenience must remain the top priorities during the festival. Senior officials were also instructed to personally inspect the arrangements and seek the assistance of Civil Defence, NCC and NSS volunteers to ensure the smooth and safe conduct of Chhath Mahaparva. (IANS Inputs)

national_raw_news.title: NCRTC to introduce fast Namo Bharat trains from Nov 16, Anand Vihar-Ghaziabad in 8 minutes
national_raw_news.content: NCRTC to introduce fast Namo Bharat trains from Nov 16, Anand Vihar-Ghaziabad in 8 minutes | Mathrubhumi English Choose Edition Change Mode NEWS COLUMNS MOVIES-MUSIC SPORTS EDUCATION FEATURES TECHNOLOGY LIFESTYLE GALLERY Astrology Home News India Namo Bharat PTI Last Updated: 14 November 2026, 04:47 PM IST 2 min Share Follow us on ❎ New Delhi: The National Capital Region Transport Corporation (NCRTC) will introduce eight additional fast Namo Bharat train services during morning and evening peak hours from November 16, reducing travel time between Anand Vihar and Ghaziabad to just eight minutes, officials said. To advertise here, Contact Us The limited-stop trains will operate on the Delhi-Meerut corridor, covering Anand Vihar to Begumpul in 36 minutes and Ghaziabad to Begumpul in 28 minutes. The entire corridor will be covered in less than 50 minutes, NCRTC said. The fast services will stop at only five stations -- Sarai Kale Khan, Anand Vihar, Ghaziabad, Begumpul and Modipuram -- to reduce travel time for commuters, particularly office-goers and students travelling during rush hours, it said. During morning peak hours, two trains in each direction will depart from Sarai Kale Khan and Modipuram at 8 am and 8.30 am. In the evening, the additional services will depart from both terminal stations at 6 pm and 6.30 pm. The eight additional trains will operate alongside regular Namo Bharat services, which will continue to run at an interval of 10 minutes, ensuring that the existing service frequency remains unchanged. The corridor currently records around 1.1 lakh daily commuters and has crossed the milestone of five crore passenger journeys. Over the past three months, the system registered an average monthly ridership of more than 32 lakh, NCRTC said. The enhanced services are also aimed at encouraging commuters to shift to public transport amid rising air pollution and reducing road congestion across the region, it stated. Passengers have been advised to check station display boards and listen to platform announcements to distinguish between fast and regular train services before boarding, it added.
